utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: We are in a position to make a ruling on the Prosecutor's motion. The motion is denied. However, in the next few days, we shall issue a detailed order setting out the strict conditions on which disclosure shall be made pursuant to Rule 66A, so that this shall be carried out 60 days before the date to be set for trial. It is a question, of course, we will discuss later on in closed session in the status conference. We may now move to our next item to be discussed in open session; namely, the request by one Defence counsel about the return of -- I have so many papers here -- about the return of the documents; I am referring to the motion filed on the 8th of May by counsel for Vlatko Kupreskic for the return of documents contained in a briefcase. I see there that this motion, that it was agreed between the Defence counsel and the Prosecutor that yesterday they would meet to try to come to some sort of agreement. I wonder whether such agreement has been reached so that we can dispose of this issue right away. Prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We have, in fact, met on a couple of occasions in the last week. The latest meeting was yesterday for the purpose of actually examining the briefcase which we had understood, through Defence counsel, was still in the possession of Mr. Kupreskic at the detention facility. A member of our staff went to the detention facility and met Defence counsel there, but it turns out that, in fact, the bag or the briefcase had been sent weeks before back to Bosnia and was not available for either party to examine. So I think it is safe to conclude that at this point there is a disagreement over what was in the bag. I think Defence counsel maintains that about 13, 14 documents were in the bag that were not returned. We have carefully reviewed our inventories and have also established a chain of custody, and we are convinced that those items were not in the bag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask Defence counsel for Vlatko Kupreskic to state his position?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In accordance with the decision of the Trial Chamber, we had two meetings with our learned colleagues from the Prosecutor's Office regarding the establishing of the possible missing of some of the contents. Finally, at our meeting yesterday, we concluded that we were not able to resolve this matter ourselves, and we presented our stance to the Prosecution; namely, that we would be informing the Trial Chamber of our position and applying to the Trial Chamber that a proper report be drawn up on the circulation, the movement of all the items contained from the date of the arrest. The accused Vlatko Kupreskic, prior to his arrest, because he had contacted and had the intention to contact this Trial Chamber, this Court, had put together all the relevant documents which he thought would count him in good stead for the Defence. Those are the documents that we are asking for today. All those documents were in his briefcase at the time of his arrest and were seized from him. When he was transferred to the detention facility, he submitted to the Prosecutor's Office that briefcase with a portion of the documents. As we know, the exact documents that were in the briefcase, we then found out subsequently that some of them were missing and asked for them to be traced. We established yesterday, without doubt, that there were 14 documents of high relevance to us that are missing. Since the answer, that these documents are not in the possession of the Prosecutor, is an answer that we consider unacceptable, and we demand that this be exactly established whether it was the representatives of the Prosecutor's Office in Sarajevo who were first in possession of these documents or perhaps are being held by this office here. As we are unable to resolve this matter in direct contact with the Prosecutor's Office, we kindly apply to the Trial Chamber to order the Prosecutor to trace the movement of the contents of the bag and who had contact with the contents of the bag from the time of their seizure in Sarajevo to this point in time. In another sentence, allow me to say why this is so essential to us. This is material proof, material evidence which the Defence considers vital and relevant and have to do with his health condition, the fact that he did not belong to any army structures and units, and documents having to do with the accused's movement at the relevant times. So if we are denied these documents, we shall be denied material evidence which is relevant to all the counts of the indictment. So I ask the Trial Chamber to make it incumbent upon the Prosecutor to trace the movement and the context in relation to the contents of the briefcase. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: Yes. We have decided that we will order the Prosecutor to submit to the Trial Chamber a report, a detailed report, tracing the movements of the contents of the briefcase or bag so that it is clear why those 14 documents are missing. Of course, no one doubts the good faith and professionalism of the Prosecution. It is probably a small hiccup somewhere that has happened, and I hope it will be possible for the Prosecution to find out where the documents are to be found so that the Defence will be handed over the 14 missing documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. In fact, we have done a search, a chain-of-custody search, to assure ourselves that no documents were missing, and, of course, I am prepared to do an oral presentation on that chain of custody today, if the Court desires, or we will be happy to submit a report as well. I might also add that it has often happened to me that I think I place something in my briefcase and I do not place it in my briefcase. So we certainly do not assume that these documents are missing as a result of anything that the Office of the Prosecutor has done. I can briefly give an overview of the chain of custody for the briefcase at this time, if the Court would desire, or we will submit a report at a later date, if the Court would desire.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CASSESE
utterances.text: It is better that you should submit a detailed written report so that we comply with the requests of the Defence counsel. We now are in a position to move to our status conference, which will be held in-camera, to go through various matters which are of great importance. I was reminded that I should set a time for the submission of the report. Could we say one week? The written report we were discussing before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MOSKOWITZ
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. --- Proceedings move into closed session status conference
